hero.title: Major Rivers and Lakes of India
hero.description: The study of major rivers and lakes is pivotal for the Allahabad High Court RO/ARO and UPPSC examinations. Questions frequently target drainage systems, origins, right and left-bank tributaries, multi-purpose river valley projects, and tectonic or oxbow lakes specific to Uttar Pradesh and India.

timeline.title: Evolutionary and Historical Milestones of Indian Drainage Systems
timeline.description: Chronological development of geological drainage phases and major water policy interventions in India.

cards.details: Upheaval of the Himalayas disrupted the ancient Shiwalik or Indo-Brahma river system, giving rise to the modern Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra drainage networks.
Construction of major canal systems such as the Upper Ganga Canal (1854) and Lower Ganga Canal to mitigate famines and boost agrarian output in the United Provinces.
Inception of massive multi-purpose river valley projects like Bhakra Nangal and Damodar Valley Corporation to harness river waters for irrigation and power.
Launch of Ganga Action Plan (GAP), followed by the establishment of the National Ganga River Basin Authority (NGRBA) in 2009 and Namami Gange Programme in 2014.

mnemonics.title: Major Rivers and Lakes of India Mnemonics & Study Tricks
mnemonics.description: Quick memory triggers to recall key facts for AHC RO/ARO exams.

items.title: Panch Prayag Order from North to South
items.phrase: V N K R D (Very Nice Karna Rudra Dev)
items.decryption: V = Vishnuprayag (Dhauliganga), N = Nandaprayag (Nandakini), K = Karnaprayag (Pindar), R = Rudraprayag (Mandakini), D = Devprayag (Bhagirathi).

items.title: West-Flowing Peninsular Rivers
items.decryption: M = Mahi, A = Aravali / Narmada, T = Tapi (Mahi, Narmada, Tapi flowing into Arabian Sea).

flashcards.description: Hover or click to reveal the answers. Revisit these cards to build instant recall.

items.question: Which river forms the 'Panch Prayag' in Uttarakhand before becoming the Ganga?
items.answer: Alaknanda River meets Dhauliganga, Nandakini, Pindar, Mandakini, and Bhagirathi at Vishnuprayag, Nandaprayag, Karnaprayag, Rudraprayag, and Devprayag respectively.

items.question: What is the unique geographical feature associated with Loktak Lake in Manipur?
items.answer: It contains floating circular swamps known as 'Phumdis' and houses Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating national park.

items.question: Which river flows through a rift valley and drains into the Arabian Sea?
items.answer: Narmada and Tapi (Tapti) rivers flow through rift valleys between Vindhya-Satpura and Satpura-Ajanta ranges respectively.

items.question: Where does the Gomti River originate, which flows directly through Lucknow?
items.answer: Fulhar Lake (Gomat Taal) near Madhotand in Pilibhit district, Uttar Pradesh.

traps.title: Common Exam Traps to Avoid
items: Confusing Indus Tributary Flow Direction: Aspirants often confuse Chenab as a minor stream; however, Chenab is the largest tributary of the Indus formed by Chandra and Bhaga streams in Himachal Pradesh.

Origin of Gomti vs. Ghaghra: Do not confuse Gomti (originates from a plain/lake in Pilibhit, UP) with Ghaghra (originates from Mapchachungo glacier in Tibet). Gomti is a plain-fed river while Ghaghra is Himalayan.

deepDive.title: Major Rivers and Lakes of India Core Study Notes
deepDive.description: The study of major rivers and lakes is pivotal for the Allahabad High Court RO/ARO and UPPSC examinations. Questions frequently target drainage systems, origins, right and left-bank tributaries, multi-purpose river valley projects, and tectonic or oxbow lakes specific to Uttar Pradesh and India.

sections.title: Himalayan Drainage System
sections.content:
Perennial river systems originating from the snow-clad Himalayas, featuring antecedent drainage and massive gorges.

  • Ganga River System: Originates as Bhagirathi from Gangotri Glacier; joins Alaknanda at Devprayag to form the Ganga. Total length is approx. 2,525 km, with maximum length flowing through Uttar Pradesh.
  • Yamuna River System: Longest and westernmost tributary of the Ganga, originating from Yamunotri Glacier on Bandarpunch peak. Meets Ganga at Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj.
  • Brahmaputra River System: Originates from Chemayungdung glacier near Mansarovar lake in Tibet (known as Yarlung Tsangpo). Enters India in Arunachal Pradesh as Dihang.
  • Indus River System: Flows west-northwest between the Ladakh and Zanskar ranges. Major tributaries include Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej governed by the Indus Waters Treaty (1960).
  • Major Left Bank Tributaries of Ganga in UP: Includes Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghra, Gandak, and Kosi. Gomti originates from Gomat Taal (Fulhar Lake) in Pilibhit district, Uttar Pradesh.

sections.title: Peninsular Drainage System
sections.content:
Older river systems characterized by broad, shallow valleys, non-perennial (seasonal) flow, and graded profiles.

  • Godavari River: Largest river of Peninsular India, often called 'Dakshina Ganga', originating from Trimbakeshwar in Nashik district, Maharashtra.
  • Krishna River: Second largest east-flowing peninsular river, originating near Mahabaleshwar in the Sahyadri range. Major tributaries include Tungabhadra, Ghatprabha, and Musi.
  • Narmada River: Flows westward through a rift valley between Vindhya and Satpura ranges, originating from Amarkantak plateau and draining into the Gulf of Khambhat.
  • Tapi (Tapti) River: Another major west-flowing river originating from Multai in Betul district, Madhya Pradesh, flowing through a rift valley parallel to Narmada.
  • Chambal River (UP-MP Border): Important right-bank tributary of Yamuna originating from Janapav hill (Mhow, MP). Famous for extensive badland topography (ravines) along the UP-MP border.

sections.title: Major Lakes of India and Uttar Pradesh
sections.content:
Inland water bodies categorized by origin including tectonic, glacial, oxbow, lagoon, and artificial reservoirs.

  • Wular Lake (Jammu & Kashmir): Largest freshwater lake in India, formed due to tectonic activity. Fed by the Jhelum River.
  • Chilika Lake (Odisha): Largest coastal lagoon in India and second largest in the world. Designated as India's first Ramsar wetland site.
  • Fulhar Lake (Pilibhit, UP): A prominent oxbow lake located in Madhotand, Pilibhit district, serving as the primary source of the Gomti River.
  • Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar: India's largest artificial man-made lake/reservoir, formed behind the Rihand Dam on the Rihand River in Sonbhadra district, UP.
  • Loktak Lake (Manipur): Largest freshwater lake in Northeast India, famous for floating decomposed plant materials called 'phumdis' and Keibul Lamjao National Park.

sections.title: River Interlinking & Major Water Projects
sections.content:
Strategic engineering interventions designed to transfer surplus water from flood-prone basins to water-deficit regions.

  • Ken-Betwa Link Project: First project under the National Perspective Plan for river interlinking. Transfers water from Ken River to Betwa River, benefiting Bundelkhand region across UP and MP.
  • Tehri Dam Project: Highest dam in India (260.5 meters) built on Bhagirathi River in Uttarakhand, serving multi-purpose irrigation and hydroelectric power generation.
  • Sardar Sarovar Project: Massive concrete gravity dam on the Narmada River in Gujarat, supplying drinking water and irrigation to Gujarat, MP, Maharashtra, and Rajasthan.
  • Matatila Dam: Constructed on the Betwa River in Lalitpur district, Uttar Pradesh, serving joint irrigation interests of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.
